note: These cases specify obligations for downstream consensus engines and relying-party verifiers. This repository has no such runtime; declaration and bounded quorum-set tests do not execute these protocol cases. given/expect use semantic test notation, not wire fields or registered decision enums. Unless stated otherwise, the authenticated committee is [A,B,C,D,X], N=5, f=1, q=4, at most X is Byzantine, and all independent authorization and reviewed-protocol conditions pass. Distinct voters are authenticated identities, not message counts. A positive case means eligible only after all required checks, not an unconditional action grant.

vectors.reason: Three-vote groups can intersect only at the Byzantine member; 2q-N must exceed f.
The arithmetic is valid, but protocol review, signatures, independence, persistence, and runtime behavior remain separate obligations.
Only X double-votes, but neither candidate has the required four distinct votes. Reproduce selective message delivery through both required phases.
One unavailable member need not block a valid protocol run among four mutually communicating members.
Repeated messages, repeated signatures, and aliases for one identity do not create a fourth vote.
Cryptographic validity does not enroll an identity in the authenticated committee.
Run once per mismatch. Every counted vote must bind the same authenticated decision context.
A prepared proposal is not a committed decision; signatures from different protocol phases cannot be combined.
Run once per failure. An invalid fourth vote leaves insufficient authenticated participation.
Availability loss pauses protected updates; the denominator remains five.
One malicious member and one separate outage can prevent progress. Safety does not permit a lower quorum.
Restarting cannot erase a prior vote or lock and allow an honest identity to equivocate.
Run once per case. Health does not establish safe recovery; verified durable state or the reviewed protocol's recovery procedure is required.
A later view must preserve committed decisions through authenticated carry-forward evidence.
Uptime and timeout are not authority to replace the selected protocol's leader-change rules.

vectors.reason: An isolated group cannot appoint its own smaller electorate, including during an emergency.
Old approval alone does not prove that the new committee has safely installed the common committed state.
Candidate members cannot authorize their own succession without the incumbent committed transition.
Run once per mismatch. Both configurations must certify the same transition and continuity boundary.
A supported joint transition can change membership without creating independently active conflicting histories.
Historical verification of an old certificate does not authorize new decisions after its configuration's activation boundary.
Enough signing shares do not establish a unique committed history.
Preserve evidence and investigate; timestamp, longest log, and administrator preference cannot repair a violated safety assumption.
Two groups of four can overlap only in faulty members; at least five votes are required.
Consensus availability does not change the proof's independent expiry boundary or authorize a stale proof.
The consensus floor does not lower a stronger operation-specific approval or signing requirement.
A shape-valid weaker digest does not satisfy the trusted Level 3 SHA-384 requirement.
A valid declaration cannot establish its own root of authority.
Distinct labels do not prove independence. Deployment assessment must account for actual shared control.
Four meets the arithmetic minimum for this topology, but cannot replace the authenticated configuration's stricter quorum of five.
Naming a protocol or checking quorum arithmetic is insufficient when its safety argument does not cover the selected deployment.
Safety remains mandatory during arbitrary delay. Progress depends on the reviewed protocol's communication and timing assumptions.
